newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Moody's outlook lift for Sweden over - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Moody's outlook lift for Sweden over - analysts.

text.p: U.S. rating agency Moody's improved outlook for Sweden's sovereign rating boosted the Swedish currency and debt markets on Friday, but analysts said the positive effects were probably over.

Ten-year Swedish bond yields fell five basis points to 6.62 percent by 1415 GMT, and the six month T-bill rate fell two basis points to 4.13 percent on Moody's comment and a stronger crown, dealers said.
Moody's statement on Thursday continued to lift the crown, which firmed to 4.4440 against the mark compared to 4.4595 late on Thursday, dealers said.
"It was Moody's that sparked interest among foreign investors, and we have seen more foreigners than Swedes buying crowns today," one chief currency dealer told Reuters.
Moody's said the outlook for Sweden's rating has improved after the country consolidated public finances over the past two years.
It said the government regained a large degree of credibility thanks to the sharp drop in the fiscal deficit, sustained low inflation and large current account surpluses.
"This is overdue given the transformation Sweden has undergone the past three years in terms of fundamentals and the fiscal situation," said Merrill Lynch economist Dick Woodworth.
Analysts said Moody's would likely upgrade Sweden, which is currently rated Aa3 for long-term foreign currency. But they did not expect an upgrade to have a large effect on Swedish debt yields.

"The effect of the positive outlook is quite small. Even if Moody's would raise Sweden's credit rating, the effect would only be five to seven basis points," Salomon Brothers economist Wike Groenenberg said.
Analysts said Sweden's improved outlook was already mostly discounted in the market.
"This can be seen in the decreased spread between longer Swedish and German bond yields," said Groenenberg.
The spread between German and Swedish long bond yields dipped below 100 basis points this week for the first time since January.
Moody's credit rating for Sweden was lower than rival Standard & Poor's (S&P) double A plus with a stable outlook. But S&P puts more weight on fundamentals while Moody's looks more at debt ratios.
"Moody's has been out of line with domestic fundamentals and the outlook. They should really raise Sweden's credit rating right away," said PaineWebber economist James McKay.
"I believe we can expect an upgrade over the next months. But I don't think it will benefit debt yields by more than 10 basis points," McKay said.
Moody's has only recently begun giving outlooks for sovereign debt ratings.
